terms.comment: mālus, with a long ā, is an upright pole or beam (Front. Strat. 3.8.3), above all a ship’s mast, and the pole that held the awnings over a theatre (Lucr. 6.110; Liv. 39.7.8; all from Lewis & Short). Andresian is the only source for the phrase; Morgan–Owens has the heading telephone pole but no word.

sources: Lewis & Short: malus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 308, checked against the searchable text of the book (11 November 2026).
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. telephone pole (heading only).
